key_insight: A deep truncated FBSDE solver stabilizes high-dimensional PDE learning by decoupling strongly coupled dynamics with gradient truncation, fictitious-play averaging, and pathwise consistency shortcuts.
engineering_relevance: The method offers a more robust numerical tool for convection-dominated and strongly coupled PDEs, improving reliability for computational science workflows where standard deep FBSDE solvers can become unstable.
method: Gradient-truncated iterative decoupling reduces unstable feedback from parameter-dependent forward paths.
Fictitious-play averaging preserves coupled dynamics while separating forward and backward updates.
Pathwise consistency loss adds local gradient shortcuts to help mitigate vanishing gradients.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports residual-based error estimates, conditional convergence of fully discrete approximations, and numerical experiments showing improved accuracy and stability across low- and high-dimensional, strongly coupled cases.
watch_item: The convergence guarantee is conditional and the pathwise consistency term is not required for the theory, so practical performance may depend on tuning and problem structure.
paper_title: Deep Truncated FBSDE Method: A Robust Solver for High-Dimensional Nonlinear PDEs and Fully Coupled FBSDEs
